goal:
You are a strict documentation reviewer for C:/Projects/DS/DS_RPC/README.md. Judge it ONLY as a first-time real user of the DRPC .NET RPC library would. You must NOT modify any files — read-only review.

Read README.md fully, then verify claims against ground truth in this repo:
- Document/03-Reference/Public-API.md (authoritative API surface)
- Document/01-Overview/Feature-Spec.md (implemented features F1-F9, F11-F14)
- Sandbox/Sandbox.Contracts, Sandbox/Sandbox.Server, Sandbox/Sandbox.Client (working example code)
- Directory.Build.props (versions)

Evaluate:
1. Quick Start viability: using ONLY the README, could a new user go from empty project to a working client->server RPC round-trip? All steps present, in order, with correct real API names/signatures/namespaces?
2. Completeness: ALL implemented features documented — five delivery modes, OneWay, server->client reverse calls, DTO [NonIdMessage], group polymorphism, [GenericProcedure], per-call TimeoutMs, Validation gate, DTLS encryption, error model, NuGet install, Unity/netstandard2.1 note?
3. Accuracy: no invented APIs, wrong parameter names, wrong versions, overstated claims?
4. Clarity: confusing jumps, unexplained jargon, leftover Korean text, broken Markdown?

Output format — EXACTLY:
First line: CLEAN if a first-time user could succeed with this README and nothing MUST be fixed; otherwise ISSUES.
If ISSUES: numbered, concrete, actionable items — quote the offending text and say what to change. No style nitpicks that do not affect a real user; no scope expansion beyond README.md.
summary:
Verification complete. All ground truth checked: Public-API.md, Feature-Spec.md (F1–F9, F11–F14), Sandbox source, Directory.Build.props, plus a live Release build/test run.

ISSUES

1. **[Major — wrong compatibility claim]** Intro paragraph: *"All runtime packages target `netstandard2.1` (the source generator targets `netstandard2.0`), so they are usable from .NET Framework, modern .NET, and Unity targets that support netstandard2.1."* — `netstandard2.1` is **not** consumable by .NET Framework (Framework tops out at netstandard2.0; NuGet restore fails with NU1202). Verified TFMs in `Source/Directory.Build.props` (`netstandard2.1`) and `Source/DRPC.CodeGenerator` (`netstandard2.0`). Fix: drop ".NET Framework" from the list (or reword to "modern .NET and netstandard2.1-capable targets such as Unity 2021.2+"). The later "Packages and Requirements" section already phrases it correctly ("Unity and other `netstandard2.1`-capable frameworks"), so only the intro sentence is wrong.

2. **[Moderate — Quick Start gap]** Step 0 sets up a separate *"Contract project (shared by both sides)"*, but no step tells the user to reference the contract project from the client/server app projects. A first-time user following the walkthrough literally gets compile errors (`IGameServerProcedures` not found) at steps 2–3. Fix: add one line to step 0, e.g. `dotnet add ./Client reference ../Contracts/Contracts.csproj` (and same for Server), consistent with `Sandbox/Sandbox.Server/Sandbox.Server.csproj` which contains `<ProjectReference Include="..\Sandbox.Contracts\Sandbox.Contracts.csproj" />`.

Everything else verified accurate against ground truth:

- **Quick Start viability (core loop):** all API names/signatures/namespaces check out — `IServerProcedureDeclarations`/`IClientProcedureDeclarations` in `DRPC.Shared.Interface` (`Document/03-Reference/Public-API.md` §계약 인터페이스), `ServerHub<,>` in `DRPC.Server.Network`, `ClientHub<,>` in `DRPC.Client.Network`, `ListenAsync(port, key, onConnect...
